transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I’m exhausted all the time, like I’m running on empty no matter how much I rest. I just don’t have the energy to keep up with anything anymore. It feels like I'm completely drained every single day.
Over the past two weeks, have you also been feeling down or lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

It’s actually been going on for well over a year, this deep down feeling where I just don't care about anything anymore. I've completely stopped touching my fishing rods, my woodshop in the garage is abandoned, and I've let my garden go. Now, I mostly just sit in my recliner staring at the wall because everything feels empty and pointless.
Over the past year, have you also had changes in your sleep or appetite, such as sleeping much more or less than usual or eating much more or less than usual?

Yes, my appetite has really dropped off over the past year, and I mostly just pick at toast or a can of soup, which has made me lose enough weight to tighten my belt a couple of notches. As for sleep, no matter how early I go to bed, I still wake up feeling completely exhausted, like I've already worked a double shift.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when these symptoms went away, or is this low mood and loss of interest present most of the time for the past year or longer?

No, it hasn't gone away at all. This dark, empty feeling has pretty much been my baseline for over a year now, ever since they announced the restructuring at work. I haven't had any real break from it where I felt like my old self again.
Have you ever had a similar depressive episode in the past that lasted at least two weeks and then fully improved, even if it was years ago?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. These heavy feelings only started recently, since I had to start planning for retirement and heard about the restructuring at work.
Have these symptoms been present for at least two weeks continuously, and did they start before or after the work restructuring and retirement stress?

Yes, they've been going on continuously for way longer than two weeks—it's been well over a year now without any real break. They definitely started right after the restructuring at work was announced and I began stressing about retirement, not before that.

Have you ever had a period of at least several days where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, talked more than usual, or did risky things that were out of character for you?

No, I've never had anything like that happen. If anything, I've felt the exact opposite—just completely drained, heavy, and low. I certainly haven't had any bursts of high energy or done anything risky.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 years when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most days, even if the symptoms were less severe than they are now?

No, I've never had a two-year stretch of feeling depressed or like this in the past. These feelings of depression and losing interest only started about a year and a half ago when the restructuring at work was announced. Before that, I generally felt fine and was active with my hobbies and work.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to work, take care of yourself, or get through daily activities, and have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living or of hurting yourself?

Yes, I've been missing shifts, letting my house go, and my supervisor even warned me because I'm falling so far behind. On the hardest nights, I find myself wishing I wouldn't wake up, and I've pictured driving off the highway or taking my blood pressure pills, though I don't have any real plan to do it.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 years when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most days, even if it was less severe than this current episode?

No, like I said, I've never experienced anything like this long-term depression before this current period started. Before the news about the restructuring at work, I was doing just fine and keeping busy with my hobbies.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life, and if so, do you have a specific plan or access to anything you could use?

I have to admit, there are nights when I lie in bed and just hope I don't wake up the next morning. I've pictured things like driving my car off the highway or taking all of my blood pressure pills. But I don't have an actual plan, and I haven't gone through with setting anything up.
Have there been any periods of at least 2 months during the past year and a half when your mood and interest in things were back to normal, or has it been low almost every day the whole time?

No, I haven't had any periods like that at all—it's been low almost every single day. I've just felt completely stuck in this heavy, drained state for over a year straight since the restructuring was announced, with no breaks where things went back to normal.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t, or had strong beliefs that others said were not true?

It's hard to talk about, but at night when I'm alone, I often hear a low male voice whispering my name and calling me a failure. I've also become convinced that management at work is secretly tracking everything I do and say, even in my own home, to make sure they can push me out.
Have the voices or beliefs about being tracked only happened during this depressed period, or have they ever occurred when your mood was otherwise normal?

There was a brief stretch earlier this year when my mood lifted slightly and I could actually find some joy in seeing my grandson. But even during those weeks when I didn't feel quite as depressed, the whispering voice at night and the feeling that management was tracking me kept happening anyway.
Have the voices or beliefs that you are being tracked ever continued for at least 2 weeks when you were not feeling depressed at all, or do they only happen during the depressed periods?

Yes, there was a period earlier this year for a few weeks where my mood lifted a bit and I wasn't feeling deeply depressed. But even during that time, the voice at night and the belief that management was tracking me kept going just the same.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when the voices or beliefs about being tracked continued even though your mood was completely normal and you were not feeling depressed at all?

Yes, there was a stretch of a few weeks earlier this year where my mood lifted and I didn't feel depressed—I even actually enjoyed seeing my grandson. But even though I felt normal then, the voice at night and the belief that management was tracking me kept going just the same. It was really confusing to have those things happen when I was otherwise feeling okay.
Have you had a period of at least 2 years when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most days, even if the symptoms were less severe than they are now?

No, it hasn't been quite two years yet. I have been feeling this way steadily for about a year and a half, ever since the restructuring at my job was first announced. Before that, I didn't have any issues with my mood or losing interest like this.
Have you had depressed mood or loss of interest most days for at least 2 years, or has it been shorter than that?

Like I mentioned, it hasn't quite been two years yet, but it has been going on steadily for about a year and a half now. It all started right after they announced the restructuring and retirement plans at my job, and I've been stuck in this state ever since.
Have your depressive symptoms lasted continuously for at least 2 years, or has it been less than 2 years overall?
It’s been less than two years overall, about a year and a half now. It all started right after they announced the restructuring at my job, and I've just been stuck in this heavy fog ever since.
Have the voices or beliefs that you are being tracked ever continued for at least 2 weeks when you were not feeling depressed at all, or do they only happen when your mood is low?

Yes, they definitely continued even when my mood wasn't low. There was a stretch of a few weeks earlier this year when I felt okay and could enjoy seeing my grandson, but the voice and the tracking still went on just the same.
Have you ever had hallucinations or fixed beliefs like the voice or being tracked for at least 2 weeks when you were not feeling depressed at all?

Yes, that's correct. There was a stretch of a few weeks earlier this year when my mood wasn't quite as heavy and crushing, and I could actually enjoy spending time with my grandson. But even during those weeks, the voice still whispered my name at night and I was still completely convinced that management was tracking me.

He also has clear psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions) that persisted for at least 2 weeks during a period when mood had improved and was not depressed, which supports schizoaffective disorder rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features.
